reviews.text: They had small birds and small animals like rabbits. The shop was clean and had a good selection, but the prices were quite high. When I tried to buy a budgie, I was told, "We can't sell it to you unless you buy the same food as well." The food seemed to be a luxury item and was expensive; the budgie was 7,000 yen, but the food cost 6,000 yen 💸. There might be a reason, like they won't eat anything else, but I was really surprised to be forced to buy it. They should clearly state that purchasing the specified food is mandatory.

Cockatiels, some of which are several years old, are being sold for 60,000-70,000 yen. They're so pitiful, completely ignored. The price is also quite high compared to other products, yet they're just gathering dust.

I looked around at several stores, including home improvement centers, to find a place to buy a hamster, and I was glad I came here because it was quite different. They treat the hamsters not just as merchandise, but as hamsters themselves, and there are staff members who seem to love animals. When I bought my hamster, they also talked to me about after-sales service, so I ended up buying a few supplies as well.
There aren't many items.

I used to think this store was kind to animals.

However, since the recent renovation, the treatment of small animals has become terrible.

The way they're displayed, almost like products, broke my heart and made me dizzy. What's the purpose of those dazzling spotlights on the cages?

Rabbits were placed in smaller cages than before, right next to the entrance. The rabbits flinched at the opening and closing of the automatic door, their eyes wide open. The lights were too bright, and they seemed stressed the whole time.

Two baby rabbits chased each other around, probably due to stress, and were shedding a lot of fur.

If you care even a little about the animals' well-being, could you please return to the previous environment?

I used to think this was a really good store, and I even adopted a hamster from there.

Now, it makes me so sad to pass by this store that I hesitate to even go near it.

I sincerely hope for improvement.

I was looking for regular hamster pellets, but unfortunately, the store mainly stocked mixed foods and diet products, with very few regular pellets available.

I was also surprised to see that the hamster food sold in stores seemed to use mixed foods. Personally, I want to feed my hamsters nutritionally balanced pellets as their main food, so I would like to see a wider variety of regular pellets available.

I raise a parrot, and while wandering around Namba Parks, I spotted some babies. They were so cute, so I went into P2 Pet Supplies to browse their merchandise!

Perhaps because Japan has a culture of enjoying keeping pet birds, the cages were clean and the babies were well cared for. They were selling birds ranging from just one month old to 3 to 6 months old!

The range of items for each animal was truly diverse. I was especially pleased to see so many parrot-related toys, perches, food, and supplements that aren't commonly found in Korea!

I just did some window shopping, but I regret not buying at least a few toys.
They were selling catnip-infused hand cream for a limited time! They have rabbits, hamsters, parakeets, tropical fish, and more! There are also lots of cute dog and cat goods!

Very cute store! The animal enclosures are a little small compared to western standards, but look very good for japanese standards. Gopd variaty of snacks, toys and other goods. Live fish, reptiles, rodents, bunnies and birds.

I sent the following email to the pet shop (which addresses my review):

Good day
Three days ago, we were at Namba Park and walked past your shop.

I was appalled by the conditions in which the birds and rabbits were kept!

The bird cages are far too small. For a pair of birds, the cage/aviary should be at least 120 cm wide, 60 cm deep, and 100 cm high. In the small cage, they have hardly any room to move around. There is also too little/no space for branches and toys.

The birdcages you sell are also much too small.

The same applies to the rabbit cages: they are far too small! The rabbits have no room to hop around. They need plenty of space. Furthermore, the rabbits should not be kept alone: ​​rabbits need the company of other rabbits for grooming, communication, and enrichment. They also lack any places to retreat to, such as a cave or a small house.

I earnestly and sincerely urge you to reconsider and adjust the living conditions of your animals. They are living beings, not display pieces. Appropriate husbandry is essential, and this also entails the responsibility of teaching a buyer how to provide appropriate care.

Thank you for your understanding and with best regards,
Rebecca Koenig
We carry cat and dog food that's hard to find elsewhere. We've recently revamped our selection and it's even better now.

A super large pet supply store in Namba
Lots of clothes and accessories for cats and dogs, and a wide variety of snacks too.
Surprisingly, there aren’t many grooming tools — not even nail clippers!
There are a few combs available, but only a small selection.

On the other side of the store, there are areas for hamsters, rabbits, fish, and birds.
You can usually find what you're looking for. They don't stock low-quality goods, so you can browse with peace of mind.
Beautifully renovated.
The products are a little cheaper than in Taiwan.

Vitality Source Papaya Enzyme and Probiotics are available in large packs, and the prices are cheaper than in Taiwan when converted to NTD. Two packs of each will last a long time. The shop assistants are very nice!
Terrible customer service

I was so annoyed when, after filling out all the paperwork to buy a hamster, they told me, "You can't buy the animal unless you also buy food (2500 yen)."
Doesn't that violate some kind of law?
By the way, the hamster I bought was cute, but it often made a sputtering coughing sound and died in less than six months.
A hamster I bought from another store has lived for over two years, so it wasn't my fault.

Frankly speaking, the attitude of the staff in charge of small animals is terrible for a store that deals with animal ecology. I can't believe that someone who claims to know nothing about animal ecology is actually in charge of the animals. This is a poor store that displays small animals like ornaments until 9 PM, even though they are still under observation.
I wish they would stop displaying and selling animals behind glass. It's so sad for the rabbits and rats because they have nowhere to hide.

As a rabbit owner, I went to browse rabbit supplies.

It was easy to find as it is not far from the escalator on the 5th floor of Namba Parks Department Store.

They had a wide variety of pet supplies available, including not only dog ​​and cat items but also supplies for rabbits, small animals, and parrots.

If you are looking to browse rabbit supplies in Osaka, I think it would be a good idea to stop by for a quick look.

I was so grateful that they had food reserved for my Java sparrows. ☺
They also offer mail order, which is very helpful.
They have the best selection of bird-related products.
They have a wide variety of products, including less common cat carriers, and the bird and rabbit carriers are very cute.
There was a wide variety of products, so it was fun to browse, and the prices were reasonable!
Spiral Perch

Regarding raising hamsters, you should absolutely avoid mixing their regular food with other foods. 
All pet shops only sell pellets, but this one is different. They are prone to becoming obese from a young age, and they can become very picky about what they eat. It would be sad if they were selling them without knowing this basic, obvious information. This is what they say at the hospital too. You should feed them pellets as their main food, and give them the food they are currently giving them as snacks.

I bought some aquatic plants, but the packaging was poor and they leaked in my bag. Considering the price, I expect better packaging.
If it had been live animals, they would have all died.
It is a good place to visit anytime before heading out.
The goods are plentiful and exquisite, but the prices are higher than elsewhere.
My hamster was sleeping in the futon! \(^o^)/ So cute!
My dog ​​loves the snacks sold here, so we come here every time. Tax-free is available! Just tell them you want tax-free, pay, and head up to the 7th floor!

This is a store for beginners in tropical fish keeping. They also sell animals, but I used it specifically for tropical fish, so I'll only write about that. They were very helpful, explaining things like which fish species can't be kept together, even for beginners. Thank you!

We ordered the product to pick up in this store, and seems no one did anything after we ordered and our product didn’t arrived at all

What a bad experience
Wasted our time travelling to this shop

Don’t come
A must-visit place in Osaka for guinea pig supplies

They have a wide variety of dog treats, food, and accessories. The treats and food selection includes many high-quality and unique items.

They also carry stylish dog clothes from fashionable brands. You can find rare items that you might only find online, so it's a great place to stop by when you're in Namba.

This pet shop in Namba Parks 🦜🐹
It's a relaxing place where you can get up close and personal with adorable animals. 🥰 Nocturnal hamsters …
A pet store with food, snacks, toys, clothes, collars, etc for your pet. It got our attention because the toys looked interesting and we wanted bring something back for our dogs at home. …
